current.text: He is the projected starting point guard next to Christian Braun, Cam Johnson, Aaron Gordon and Nikola Jokic.
Experts expect him to keep about 28 usage and 35 minutes. One ranker says his role is the one he trusts most in his guard tier.
Under coach David Adelman his usage rose to 28. Many teammate absences helped, since he was the only one who stayed healthy.
His 42 to 43% three-point shooting from his career-best season will probably drop.
Lloyd thinks he could finish inside the top 14. Other calls put him between top 12 and 14, and say he could finish above Tyrese Maxey.

Experts call his ESPN rank, around 28 to 37 in their videos, far too low. They call him safe in the middle of round two and fine as early as the start of round two. He also pairs well with Jokic there.
In an expert auction mock, Josh targeted him with a 34 USD maximum. He sold for 37 USD.
Moore thinks Denver could trade him by the deadline to shed salary, because it cannot build a top-15 defense while paying both Jokic and Murray over 30M USD.
Moore expects at least two of last year's Denver starters to be gone by the deadline. He doubts ownership will pay the luxury tax.
Denver has 43 games through March 28, one below the maximum. It has only 14 back-to-backs, one of the lowest counts in the league. It also has one of only three five-game weeks this season.
Moore doubts Denver will rest Murray, Jokic and Gordon on purpose. He predicts about 50 wins.
Denver is pretty healthy heading into the season.

durable.text: He is a strong three-point shooter, close to 40% or better over the last four years. Around 40 to 41% is a reasonable expectation going forward.
His game has moved toward playmaking, closer to Tony Parker than a discount Steph Curry. He gives volume scoring, threes, good assists and a good FG% for a guard.
He is strong in PTS, AST, 3PM and FT%, with no category weak enough to punt.

note: Murray fits every build: he helps in PTS, AST, 3PM and FT% and has no weak category. Experts see a top 12 to 14 finish, above both his Yahoo rank (17) and his ESPN rank (22). Yahoo values him at 40 USD (average cost 39.2) while ESPN buyers pay only 24.8 USD, and he went for 27 USD in our league last season, so he could come cheaper than his Yahoo value. Paying in the mid to high 30s is in line with the expert mock (34 USD maximum, sold at 37 USD). Early in the season, check whether he keeps about 28 usage now that his teammates are healthy, whether his three-point shooting drops back toward 40%, and any trade talk before the March 4 deadline.
